title: How Final Fantasy XIV Survived Its Shutdown
first_frame_text: How Final Fantasy XIV Survived Its Shutdown
hook: On November 11, 2012, Eorzea went dark under producer and director Naoki Yoshida. Final Fantasy 14 had damaged the series' reputation and cost Square Enix its players' trust. The original game was finished. Its replacement would arrive in August 2013. Getting Eorzea back was only the beginning. Why weren't patches enough for Square Enix to save the original game? And did that relaunch become a commercial success? Final Fantasy 14's second chance meant convincing you that the company behind its failure deserved another monthly payment. This documentary follows how it earned that chance. Rapture was the codename when Square Enix began planning its next online Final Fantasy in 2005. Producer Hiromichi Tanaka had already produced Final Fantasy 11. Square Enix was committing another numbered Final Fantasy to life online.
take_narration: Final Fantasy 14 earned its second chance because Square Enix replaced the foundations that had failed. Yoshida's team gave the replacement a new engine and improved server infrastructure. Controller play became a priority. Final Fantasy 14 A Realm Reborn delivered the promised PS3 version alongside its Windows release. Today, its commercial success is settled history. Square Enix credited its sales and subscribers with helping restore profitability in 2014. The Legacy Campaign also rewarded players who paid for at least three months with permanently lower subscription fees. Eorzea's servers closed on November 11. Rebuilding that world gave players a reason to return. That's the Pulse. Play something good this week.

title: Why San Andreas Never Got a Sequel

hook: Grove Street can pull you back to Grand Theft Auto San Andreas, but a familiar city can mislead your next purchase. You need more than an address. Why didn't CJ's story continue in Rockstar's next GTA? San Andreas was originally planned as three maps linked by public transport. A modder in the Netherlands used a hex editor to unlock hidden content. Grand Theft Auto 4 paired a smaller city with a budget above $100 million. Grand Theft Auto 5 left San Fierro and Las Venturas out of its return. We've checked the published development history, release dates, map changes and story continuity. Last, we'll reach CJ's return and see exactly what Rockstar brought back for you. The answer starts with extra time. Rockstar North had room to experiment.
take_narration: Rockstar moved into a newer narrative continuity, then rebuilt Los Santos within it. The city returned; CJ's story stayed behind. GTA 4 favored a smaller, more detailed city. GTA 5 took that approach back to Los Santos. For you, familiar place names connect games whose stories belong to different continuities. You can revisit CJ through Grand Theft Auto The Trilogy The Definitive Edition, announced on October 8, 2021. Grove Street Games revised the controls and rebuilt the lighting around his original adventure. Rockstar published the collection. His journey remains the same. Grove Street still takes you into CJ's original story. The familiar address leads back to his beginning. That's the Pulse. Play something good this week.
